author: Signal Enhancer maintainers with Codex source review <https://github.com/sergiopesch/signal-enhancer>

statements.impact_statement: Boundary: the worker performs no pathname ACL operation and runs without privilege as UID/GID 10001, so an attacker cannot direct a privileged acl_*_file call. Evidence: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-54369 Reassess: on any ACL or base-image change.

Boundary: the worker invokes no getfacl, setfacl, chacl, or privileged pathname ACL operation and runs as UID/GID 10001. Evidence: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-54370 Reassess: on any ACL or base-image change.

Boundary: the worker never calls the deprecated resolver-debug functions, and CI inventories every final-image ELF before audit-tool installation, verifies it remains byte-identical, and fails on imports or non-provider symbol strings for ns_printrrf, ns_printrr, or fp_nquery. Evidence: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-5435 Reassess: on any native dependency, audit, glibc, or base-image change.

Boundary: the flaw is confined to the infocmp CLI. The fixed audio service and launcher never invoke infocmp, and no API parameter controls terminal or terminfo input. The launcher permission-denial probe uses only a fixed dpkg-deb command. Evidence: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-69720 Reassess: on any infocmp invocation, terminal/terminfo input, native tooling, ncurses, source or base-image change.

Boundary: both Debian libsndfile and SoundFile 0.13.1's bundled libsndfile 1.2.2 are present, but the worker's bounded RIFF parser rejects IMA ADPCM (format 0x0011) and every codec except PCM/float before passing only tensors to the model; tests pin this rejection. Evidence: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-37555 Reassess: on any WAV parser, SoundFile, libsndfile, model-adapter, or base-image change.

Boundary: Debian perl-base does not ship Archive::Tar, and the worker does not invoke Perl or extract archives. Evidence: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/amd64/perl-base/filelist Reassess: on any Perl package or base-image change.

Boundary: this assessment is limited to the matched Debian gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1 and libstdc++6 runtime packages. Their actual SBOM-owned files contain no PBDS binary_heap erase_if header implementation; the upstream fix changes that header template. The final-image guard also rejects any shipped binary_heap_/erase_fn_imps.hpp. This does not certify unrelated native wheels or their inlined C++ templates. Evidence: https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/aaa8351f4d2e636f9680a1f0a8ebc2f0a60611e6 Reassess: on any GCC/runtime/header, native dependency, image or source-boundary change.

Boundary: within this immutable built image, the fixed audio service and all original ELFs have no permitted imported or non-provider runtime lookup of strfmon, strfmon_l, __strfmon_l or __vstrfmon_l. Two exact-hash NVRTC builtin-name records are separately bound to their sole offsets, names, type table and RELATIVE relocations; actual imports remain forbidden. Provider-injected native libraries are outside this assessment and require a fresh runtime boundary audit before promotion. The glibc provider itself remains unpatched. Evidence: https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0017 Reassess: on any source, native library, metadata classifier, loader, provider runtime or base-image change.

Boundary: for these exact matched util-linux binary packages, the approved fixed audio service invokes no privileged mount, external mount helper or X-mount/fstab post-hook operation. The actual image strips all set-ID/file capabilities; its fixed launcher requires UID/GID10001, zero process capabilities and no-new-privileges, and provider/image validation rejects command and environment overrides. This does not assess privileged operator mount use outside that service boundary or claim util-linux patched. Evidence: https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-m25x-3hj9-m26f Reassess: on any mount/helper/fstab use, privilege, launcher, provider command, package or base-image change.

Boundary: the approved fixed audio service and deployment path never invoke privileged nsenter --join-cgroup against an attacker-controlled target. The exact USER/command/entrypoint and provider allowlists exclude that path. The launcher also closes inherited descriptors above2 before fixed exec; stdin/stdout/stderr0-2 intentionally remain. UID/capability drops or no-new-privileges alone are not the rationale: root-opened cgroup descriptors retain authority. This does not assess a privileged operator entering an attacker namespace or changing that launch boundary. Evidence: https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-55fx-f4gg-cfhj Reassess: on any privileged nsenter/cgroup/namespace entry, inherited-descriptor contract, provider/command override, package or base-image change.

Boundary: for these exact matched util-linux binary packages, the fixed audio service performs no privileged mount or X-mount.subdir detached-tree operation on attacker-controlled paths. Set-ID and file capabilities are stripped; the launcher verifies UID/GID10001, zero process capabilities and no-new-privileges. Fixed image/provider commands reject alternate namespace or mount entry paths. Privileged operator use outside the approved service is not assessed, and util-linux is not claimed patched. Evidence: https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-8f2p-47x3-43mv Reassess: on any mount/subdir/namespace use, privileges, command override, package or base-image change.

Boundary: for these exact matched util-linux binary packages, the fixed audio service performs no privileged restricted bind mount or X-mount.owner/group/mode action. Set-ID/file capabilities are stripped, the launcher requires UID/GID10001, zero process capabilities and no-new-privileges, and provider/image commands cannot override the fixed entry. This excludes the required privileged mount/source-redirection path; it does not assess privileged operator use or claim util-linux patched. Evidence: https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-rh77-686x-2f2m Reassess: on any mount/fstab/owner-hook use, privilege, command, package or base-image change.

Boundary: the exact matched Debian perl-base package in this immutable image does not ship Pod::Text or its Color, Overstrike and Termcap wrappers. Its actual SBOM owns617 files with no Pod/Text implementation, consistent with the Debian file list. The final-image guard rejects Text.pm/.pmc, the complete Pod/Text tree and module aliases; the fixed audio service does not invoke Perl or format POD. Evidence: https://github.com/rra/podlators/commit/70510174f69eb54aa6d617bde4e1402cd9b7c61f Reassess: on any Perl package/module, formatter invocation, image or reviewed source-boundary change.

Boundary: this immutable image permits no gzip-file-writer call or lookup by the fixed audio service. All original ELF/source gzwrite-family references are rejected except two exact-hash root-owned mode000 package-tool consumers; UID10001 read, exec and dlopen denial, no preload/LD overrides, fixed launch and audit permission restoration are verified. The zlib provider is not claimed patched or outside the affected range. Provider-injected native libraries require a fresh runtime boundary audit before promotion. Evidence: https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148 Reassess: on any gzip writer, package-tool access, loader, provider native runtime, source or base-image change.

Boundary: before any libsndfile decoder, the worker manually parses bounded RIFF/WAVE, accepts only PCM/float, rejects MAT4 and passes only decoded numeric tensors to the fixed model. Valid little- and big-endian MAT4 fixtures are rejected at the RIFF boundary. This assessment covers only the exact matched Debian libsndfile1 product; no additional SoundFile package assessment is introduced for this CVE. The library source is not claimed patched. Evidence: https://github.com/libsndfile/libsndfile/issues/1151 Reassess: on any input parser, codec, model adapter, libsndfile or base-image change.

Boundary: the matched Debian runtime packages do not contain the vulnerable alternate-target aligned-new size-rounding path. The exact hash-pinned libstdc++ runtime calls posix_memalign with the unrounded size; the upstream fix explicitly excludes modern posix_memalign configurations. gcc-14-base and libgcc-s1 do not ship the aligned-new implementation. This is an assessment of the actual compiled runtime, not a claim that every GCC target is patched. Evidence: https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/200183d4ab5d57575f3dfebc6af3baf649910b9e Reassess: on any C++ runtime hash, GCC target/configuration, native dependency or base-image change.
